3. Except with the prior written con­
sent of the Director, no attachment by 
mesne process, garnishment, execution, 
or otherwise shall be levied on or against 
any of the real or personal property or 
other assets, tangible or intangible, in 
the possession of the Director hereunder.
4. Possession, control, and operation 
of any plant or facility, or of the trans­
portation system, or any part.thereof, or 
any real or personal property, taken 
under this order shall be terminated by 
the Director when he determines that 
such possession, control, and operation 
are no longer necessary for the success­
ful prosecution of the war.
5. For the purposes of paragraphs 1  
to 4, inclusive, of this order, there are 
hereby transferred to the Director the 
functions, powers and duties vested in 
the Secretary of War by that part of sec­
tion 1  of the said Act of August 29, 1916, 
reading as follows:
“The President, in time of war, is em­
powered, through the Secretary of War, 
to take possession and assume control 
of any system or systems of transporta­
tion, or any part thereof, and to utilize 
the same, to the exclusion as far as 
may be necessary of all other traffic 
thereon, for the transfer or transporta­
tion of troops, war material and equip­
ment, or for such other purposes in con­
nection with the emergency as may be 
needful or desirable.”
6. The Director of the Office of De­
fense Transportation may request the 
Secretary of War to furnish protection 
for persons employed or seeking employ­
ment in the plants, facilities, or trans­
portation system of which possession is
taken and to furnish protection for such 
plants, facilities, and transportation sys­
tem, and may request the Secretary of 
War to furnish equipment, manpower, 
and other facilities or services deemed 
necessary by the Director to carry out 
the provisions and purposes of this 
order; and the Secretary of War is au­
thorized and directed upon such request 
to take such action as he deems neces­
sary to furnish such protection, equip­
ment, manpower, or other facilities or 
services.

RESTRICTIONS ON DISTRIBUTION A N D  USE 
OF C O RN
The fulfillment of requirements for the 
defense of the United States will result 
in a shortage in the supply of corn for 
defense, for private account, and for ex­
port; and the following order is deemed 
necessary and appropriate in the public 
interest and to promote the national de­
fense: ..
§  1468.11 Restrictions on the distribu­
tion and use of corn —(a) Definitions.
(1) “Person” means any individual, part­
nership, association, business trust, cor­
poration, or any organized group of per­
sons whether incorporated or not.
(2) “Corn” means yellow, white, or 
mixed shelled corn, or snap corn, of the 
dent or flint varieties, in any form, in­
cluding, but not limited to, such corn, 
whether whole or crushed, or mixed with 
other grains.
(3) “Distiller” means any person en­
gaged in the business of manufactur­
ing alcohol or alcoholic beverages or spir­
its by any process which includes dis­
tillation.
(4) “Export” means the shipment of 
corn to a foreign country or the sale of 
corn to the government of a foreign coun­
try or to any other buyer whose princi­
pal place of business is in a foreign coun­
try. The term includes such a shipment 
or sale made at any time after the effec­
tive date of this order.
(5) / ‘ Futures contract” means a con­
tract of sale for future delivery of corn 
traded in on any contract market desig­
nated under the. Commodity Exchange 
Act.
(6) “Acceptance of delivery” means to 
receive custody, control, or physical pos­
session, or legal title.
(7) “Order Administrator” means the 
Chief of the Agriculaural Adjustment 
Agency, War Food Administration.
(b) Restrictions on distribution to dis­
tillers. Subject to the provisions of (d) 
hereof, on and after the effective date of 
this order, no person shall sell or contract 
to sell com to any distiller, and no dis­
tiller, or any person acting on behalf of a 
distiller, shall purchase, contract to pur­
chase, or accept delivery of corn, Pro­
vided, however,  That delivery of corn 
may be accepted by a distiller pursuant 
to a contract, other than a futures con­
tract, entered into prior to the effective 
date of this order.
(c) Restrictions on distribution for ex­
port. Subject to the provisions of (d) 
hereof, on and after the effective date of 
this order, no person shall purchase or 
contract to purchase corn for export. *
(d) Futures contracts.  The restric­
tions of (b) and (c) hereof shall not 
apply to a futures contract, Provided, 
however, That no person who, on or after 
the effective date of this order, accepts 
delivery of com pursuant to a futures 
contract shall export such corn or use 
it for the manufàcture of alcohol or alco­
holic beverages or spirits.
(e) Restrictions on export and use^  
On and after the effective date of this 
order, no person shall export corn or 
use corn for the manufacture of alcohol 
or alcoholic beverages or spirits by any 
process which includes distillation, un­
less such person acquired such corn pur­
suant to a contract, other than a futures 
contract, entered into prior to June 11, 
1945.
(f) Contracts. Except as otherwise 
provided herein, the restrictions of this 
order shall be observed without regard 
to existing contracts, or any rights ac­
crued, or payments made thereunder.
(g) Records and reports.  (1) The/ 
Order Administrator shall be entitled to 
obtain such information from and re­
quire such reports and the keeping of 
such records by, any person, as may be 
necessary or appropriate, in his discre­
tion, to the enforcement or administra­
tion of the provisions of this order, sub­
ject to the approval of the Bureau of

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10461
Delegating and Transferring Certain
Functions and Affairs to the Office
of Defense Mobilization Provided for
in Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953
By virtue of the authority vested in me
by the Constitution and the statutes, in­
cluding the Defense Production Act of
1950, as amended, and as President of
the United States and Commander in
Chief of the armed forces of the United
States, it is ordered as follows:
Section 1. The Office of Defense Mo­
bilization and the Director of the Office
of Defense Mobilization provided for in
Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953 are
hereby made in all respects the succes­
sors, respectively, of the Office of Defense
Mobilization and the Director of Defense
Mobilization provided for in Executive
Order No. 10193 of December 16, 1950
(15 F. R. 9031).

Washington, Wednesday, July 16, 1952
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10373
A m e n d in g E xecutive  O rder N o. 10161
W it h R espect  to R eal  E state  C redit
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution and statutes, in­
cluding the Defense Production Act of 
1950, as amended, and as President of 
the United States, it is ordered that 
Executive Order No. 10161 of September 
9, 1950, 15 P. R. 6105-6108, as amended, 
shall be, and it is hereby, further 
amended by adding the following at the 
end of Part V thereof :
“S ec. 503. (a) Except as otherwise 
provided in section 503 (b) of this Ex­
ecutive order, the functions conferred 
upon the President by section 607 of the 
Defense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended, are hereby delegated to the 
Board of Governors of the Federal Re­
serve System. The Board shall perform 
the functions delegated by this subsec­
tion subject to the concurrence of the 
Housing and Home Finance Administra­
tor and upon the basis of estimates made 
pursuant to section 503 (b) of this 
Executive order.
“ (b) The Secretary of Labor shall, 
pursuant to section 607 of the Defense 
Production Act of 1950, as amended, 
make estimates of the number of perma­
nent, non-farm, family dwelling units 
the construction of which has been 
started during each calendar month, 
and, on the basis of such estimates, make 
estimates of the annual rate of construc­
tion starts during each such month, 
after making reasonable allowance for 
seasonal variations in the rate of con­
struction. The Secretary shall transmit 
the said estimates to the Board of Gov­
ernors of the Federal Reserve System.
“ (c) The concurrence of the Housing 
and Home Finance Administrator speci­
fied in section 501 (b) of this Executive 
order shall not be necessary to the pre- 
* scribing, changing, or suspending of the 
provisions of any regulation of the 
Board of Governors of the Federal Re­
serve System issued pursuant to section 
501 hereof with respect to extensions of 
credit during any ‘period of residential 
credit control relaxation’ announced 
pursuant to the said section 607, and the 
requirements of section 502 (b) hereof
shall not be applicable during any such 
period.’’
H arry  S. T r um an
T h e W h it e H o use,
July 14, 1952.

```text
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Z. Lewis Dalby, Chief Counsel, United States Employees' Compensation Commission, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, see. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Z. Lewis Dalby from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 12, 1940.

```

By virtue of the authority vested in

utes of the United States, section 1 of

employees who transferred to public or  
private agencies for national-defense or  
war work, is hereby amended to read as  
follows:

positions in the Federal service acquired  
under authority of Executive Order No.  
8973 of December 12,1941, Executive Or­
der No. 9067 of February 20, 1942, or  
Directive No. X as amended by Directive

sion (7 F. R. 7298, 11050), or under regu­

issued pursuant thereto, shall expire on  
October 22, 1948, unless application for  
reemployment under such rights shall  
have been made before that date: Pro­
vided, that nothing in this order shall  
prevent the exercise of such reemploy­
ment rights on or after October 22,1848,
(a) by any employee who on that date  
is serving in a Federal agency which on  
that date is being liquidated or is re­
quired by statute to be liquidated; or (b)  
by any person upon separation from the  
armed forces or release from the mer­
chant marine if at the time of his entry 
into the armed forces or merchant ma­
riné he would have acquired restoration  
rights had he entered such service from  
the agency from which he originally  
transferred: And Provided further,  that  
any person who subsequent to October  
22, 1948, takes any action which results  
in the extension of his period of service
in the armed forces or merchant marine  
may not exercise such reemployment  
rights upon separation or release there­
from.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10324
Amending  E xecutive  O rder N o. 10161 s

age, and P ort F acilities ’*
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Defense Production Act of 1950, 
as amended (50 U. S. C. App. 2061 et 
seq.), and as President of the United 
States and Commander in Chief of the 
armed forces of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
Section  1. Paragraphs (e) and (k) of 
section 901 of Executive Order No. 10161 
of September 9, 1950 (15 F. R. 6105; 3 
CFR, 1950 Supp., p. 123), as amended, 
are hereby amended to read as follows: 
“ (e) The term ‘solid fuels’ shall mean 
all forms of anthracite, bituminous, sub- 
bituminous, andlignitic coals; coke; and 
coal chemicals.”
“ (k) The term ‘domestic transporta­
tion, storage, and port facilities’ shall 
include locomotives, cars, motor vehicles, 
watercraft used on inland waterways, in 
harbors, and on the Great Lakes, and 
other vehicles, vessels, and all instru­
mentalities of shipment or carriage, ir­
respective of ownership, and all services 
in or in connection with the carriage of 
persons or property in intrastate, inter­
state, or foreign commerce within the 
United States, its Territories and posses­
sions, and the District of Columbia, ex­
cept movement of petroleum and gas by 
pipeline; and warehouses, piers, docks, 
wharves, loading and unloading equip­
ment, and all other structures and 
facilities used in connection with the 
transshipment of persons and property 
between domestic carriers and carriers 
engaged in coastwise, intercoastal, and 
overseas transportation.’*
Sec. 2. To the extent that provisions 
of any prior Executive order are incon­
sistent with the provisions of this order, 
the latter shall control, and any such

ingly. All orders, regulations, rulings, 
certificates, directives, and other actions 
relating to any function affected by this 
order shall remain in effect except as 
they are inconsistent herewith or are 
hereafter amended or revoked under 
proper authority.
H arry S. T ruman  —
T he W hite  H ouse ,
February 6,1952.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403) 
and by section 1753 of the Revised Stat­
utes of the United States, it is hereby 
ordered as follows:
1. All existing reemployment rights to 
positions in the Federal service acquired 
under authority of Executive Order No. 
8973 of December 12,1941, Executive Or­
der No. 9067 of February 20, 1942, or
Directive No. X as amended by Directive 
No. XVI of the War Manpower Commis­
sion (7 F. R. 7298,11050), or under regu­
lations of the Civil Service Commission 
issued pursuant thereto, shall expire at 
the end of the six months’  period fol­
lowing the date of this order unless ap­
plication for reemployment under such 
rights shall have been made before the 
end of such six months’  period.
2. This order shall not affect reem­
ployment rights heretofore or hereafter 
acquired under Executive Order No. 9711 
of April 11, 1946, No. 9721 of May 10, 
1946, No. ^862 of May 31, 1947, or No. 
9932 of February 27, 1948.
3. The Civil Service Commission is au­
thorized to prescribe such rules and regr 
ulations and to establish such procedures 
as may be necessary for the administra­
tion of this order.

TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10182
Providing for the A ppointment  of C er­
tain P ersons U nder the D efense  P ro­
duction A ct of 1950 and P rescribing

By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Defense Production Act of 
1950, approved September 8,1950 (Public 
Law 774, 81st Congress), hereinafter re­
ferred to as the Act, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
P A R T  i
Section 101. (a) The head of any de­
partment or agency delegated or as­
signed functions under the Act pursuant 
to Executive Order No. 10161, of Septem­
ber 9, 1950, is hereby delegated the au­
thority provided by subsection 710 (b) of 
that Act to employ persons of outstand­
ing experience and ability without com­
pensation. The authority delegated by 
this subsection 101 (a) may not be re­
delegated.
(b) Such heads of departments or 
agencies are further delegated the au­
thority provided by subsection 710 (c) 
of that Act to employ experts and con­
sultants, or organizations thereof.
(c) Such heads of departments or 
agencies are further delegated the au­
thority provided by subsection 710 (d) 
of that Act to utilize the services of Fed­
eral, State, and local agencies and to 
utilize and establish such regional, local, 
or other agencies, and to utilize such vol­
untary and uncompensated services as 
may from time to time be needed.
Sec. 102. The head of any depart­
ment or agency delegated authority pur­
suant to subsections 101 (a) and 101 (b) 
of this Part shall be guided in the exer­
cise of that authority by the following 
policies:
(a) So far as possible, operations 
under the Act shall be carried on by full­
time, salaried employees of the Govern­
ment, and appointments under this 
authority shall be to advisory or consult­
ative positions only.
(b) Appointments to positions other 
than advisory or consultative may be 
made under this order only when the re­
quirements of the position are such that 
the incumbent must personally possess 
outstanding experience and ability not 
obtainable on a full-time, salaried basis.
(c) In the appointment of personnel 
and in assignment of their duties, the 
head of the department or agency in­
volved shall take steps to avoid, to as 
great an extent as possible, any conflict 
between the' governmental duties and 
the private interests of such personnel.
Sec. 103. The authority delegated by 
subsection 101 (c) to utilize at the re­
gional and local levels voluntary and un­
compensated services is not subject to 
the policies prescribed in section 102. 
Such authority may not be exercised, 
however, to fill positions subject to the 
Classification Act of 1949.
partii
S ec. 201. Any person employed under 
Part I of this order is hereby exempted, 
with respect to such employment, from 
the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 
434, and 1914 of Title 18, United States 
Code, and section 190 of the Revised Stat­
utes (5 U. S. C. 99), except as specified 
in the following subsections:
(a) Exemption hereunder shall not 
extend to the negotiation or execution, 
by an appointee under this order, of 
Government contracts with the private 
employer of such appointee or with any 
corporation, joint stock company, asso­
ciation, firm, partnership, or other entity 
in the pecuniary profits or contracts of 
which the appointee has any direct or 
indirect interest.(b) Exemption hereunder shall not 
extend to making any recommendation 
or taking any action with respect to in­
dividual applications to the Government 
for relief or assistance, on appeal or oth­
erwise, under the provisions of the Act 
made by the private employer of the ap­
pointee or by any corporation, joint stock 
company, association, firm, partnership, 
or other entity in the pecuniary profits 
or contracts of which the appointee has 
any direct or indirect interest.
(Continued on p. 8015)

lished document are also made:

in the third line of paragraph (b) should 
read “receive”, and in paragraph (c) the 
words “these regulations” in the second

should read “this subpart” and 
“counted”, respectively. .  Section 25.54 
as corrected reads as follows:
§  25.54 Miscellaneous provisions, (a) 
Any officer or employee receiving a rate 
of basic compensation in excess of the 
maximum scheduled rate for his grade 
in accordance with the saving clause in 
section 604 (b) (11), or section 1105 (b)^
of the Classification Act of 1949, or any 
other provision of law, shall be granted 
longevity step-increases only when they 
would have been granted under these reg­
ulations and sections 703 (c) of the Clas­
sification Act of 1949, if his salary had

### Tf80e795bfd92f8f058662c34

Text hash 5d4cc9a5433076ba92a020ace53afd8a1c9c72fbc9a48a0849cf250073f5a252; absolute characters 0–595; files: jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8257-authorizing-excepted-appointments-meet-public-exigency.txt

```text
By virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the provisions of paragraph Eighth of subdivision SECOND of Section 2 of the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403, 404), it is hereby ordered that, subject to appropriate noncompetitive tests of fitness, the Civil Service Commission is authorized to permit an immediate appointment without regard to the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Rules in any case in which it appears that a public exigency exists which is directly connected with the neutrality of the United States or the preparedness program of the Federal Government.
```

By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by the Constitution and statutes,

A G EN CY
Section  101. (a) There is hereby cre­
ated an agency which shall be known as  
the Defense Materials Procurement  
Agency. There shall be at the head of  
the said agency a Defense Materials  
Procurement Administrator, who shall  
perform his duties subject to direction,  
control, and coordination by the Di­
rector of Defense Mobilization.
(b) The Defense Materials Procure­
ment Administrator shall be appointed  
by the President by and with the advice  
and consent of the Senate, There may  
be appointed to the office of Defense Ma­
terials Procurement Administrator any  
officer of the Executive branch of the  
Government designated by the Presi­
dent, to hold the office of Defense Mate­
rials Procurement Administrator in  
addition to his other office: Provided,  
That the office of Administrator shall  
have no compensation attached to it  
so long as it is held by any other officer  
of the Government.

Executive Order No. 10161 of September  
9,1950 (15 F. R. 6105-6106) , as amended, 
are hereby revoked, and there are hereby 
inserted in lieu thereof the following  
new sections:
“S ec. 303. The Defense Materials Pro­
curement Administrator is hereby au­
thorized and directed to purchase and  
make commitments to purchase metals,  
minerals, and other materials, for Gov­
ernment use or resale, as authorized by  
and subject to the provisions of section
303 of the Defense Production Act of  
1950, as amended: Provided,  That the  
Secretary of Agriculture is also au­
thorized to exercise the said functions  
under section 303 of the said Act, as  
amended, with respect to food.
“S ec. 304. The Defense Materials Pro­
curement Administrator is hereby au­
thorized and directed to encourage the  
exploration, development, and mining of  
critical and strategic minerals and  
metals, as authorized by and subject to  
the provisions of section 303 of the  
Defense Production Act of 1950, as  
amended.
“S ec. 305. The Defense Materials Pro­
curement Administrator is hereby au­
thorized and directed to make subsidy  
payments, to determine the amounts,  
manner, terms, and conditions thereof,  
and to make findings, as authorized by  
and subject to the provisions of section  
303 (c) of the Defense Production Act  
of 1950, as amended.
“S ec. 306. The functions conferred  
upon the President by section 303 (e) of  
the Defense Production Act of 1950, as  
amended, with respect to the installa­
tion of additional equipment, facilities,  
processes, or improvements to plants,  
factories, and other industrial facilities  
owned by the United States Govern­
ment, and with respect to the installa­
tion of government-owned equipment in  
plants, factories, and other industrial  
facilities owned by private persons, are  
hereby delegated to the Defense Mate­
rials Procurement Administrator.
“S ec. 307. The functions conferred  
upon the Defense Materials Procure­
ment Administrator by sections 303 to 
306, inclusive, of this Executive order,  
shall be parried out in accordance with  
programs certified to the said Adminis­
trator by the Defense Production Ad­
ministrator: Provided,  That any exercise  
by the Defense Materials Procurement  
Administrator of the functions provided  
for in section 303 hereof with respect to  
food shall be carried out in accordance  
with programs certified to him by the  
Secretary of Agriculture.

in sections 303 to 306, inclusive, of this

FEDERALREGSTER

Washington, Wednesday,  May 6,1942
The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9156
F urther  D efining  the  F unctions  and

T ransportation
By virtue of the authority conferred 
upon me by the Constitution and statutes 
of the United States, as President of the 
United States and Commander in Chief 
of the Army and Navy, it is hereby 
ordered:
1 . In addition to the functions, duties 
and powers conferred upon it by Execu­
tive Order No. 8989, approved December 
18, 1941,1  the Office of Defense Transpor­
tation shall:
a. Include within the scope of its 
authority and responsibility, as defined in 
said order, all rubber-borne transporta­
tion facilities, including passenger cars, 
buses, taxicabs, and trucks.
b. Develop programs to facilitate the 
continuous adjustment of the Nation and 
its transport requirements to the avail­
able supply of transportation services 
relying upon rubber.
c. Formulate measures to conserve and 
assure maximum utilization of the exist­
ing supply of civilian transport services 
dependent upon rubber, including the 
limitation of the use of rubber-borne 
transportation facilities in non-essential 
civilian activities, and regulation of the 
use or distribution of such transportation 
facilities among essential activities.
2. The several Federal departments 
and agencies which perform functions 
relating to the conservation or use of 
rubber-borne transportation facilities 
shall, in discharging such functions, 
conform to such policies, programs, and 
measures as the Director of the Office of 
Defense Transportation may prescribe in 
the execution of the powers vested in him 
by this order and by Executive Order No. 
8989.
3. Nothing herein shall be deemed in 
any way to limit the functions and 
authority of the Chairman of the War

By virtue of the authority vested in me by the provisions of paragraph Eighth, subdivision SECOND, section 2 of the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403, 404), it is hereby ordered that subject to the other requirements of the Civil Service Rules, the provisions of such Rules relating to time limitations on reinstatement eligibility shall be made applicable on and after the date of this order rather than on and after the date of actual separation as to all former Federal employees who were separated from their positions during the period June 30, 1932, to July 26, 1937, solely because of the operation of section 213 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 406).

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 124A of the Internal Revenue 
Code, , and as President of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1. The Chairman of the National Se­
curity Resources Board is hereby desig­
nated as the certifying authority for the 
purposes of and within the meaning of 
section 124A of the Internal Revenue 
Code, as added by section 216 of the 
Revenue Act of 1950, approved Sep­
tember 23, 1950.
2. In carrying out his function as the 
certifying authority, the Chairman shall 
utilize departments and agencies of the 
Government according to their respec­
tive assigned responsibilities pursuant to 
the Defense Production Act of 1950, as 
follows:
(a) To furnish reports and recom­
mendations in respect of applications 
for necessity certificates relating to the 
amortization of emergency facilities.
(b) To maintain relationships with 
the various industries in respect of ap­
plications for necessity certificates.
(c) To develop necessary programs for 
the expansion of capacity.
H arry  S. T r u m an
T he  W h it e H o u s e,

SUBPART— SWEETPOTATO PURCHASE PRO­
GRAM (FISCAL YEAR 1951)
§  669.6 Sweetpotatoes (fiscal year  
1951). In order to encourage the do­
mestic consumption of sweetpotatoes by 
diverting them from the normal chan­
nels of trade and commerce in accord­
ance with section 32, Public Law 320, 
74th Congress, approved August 24,1935, 
as amended, sweetpotatoes will be pur­
chased during the fiscal year ending 
June 30, 1951, in instances where sur­
pluses exist, and subject to limitations 
imposed by the capacity of available out­
lets to utilize supplies without waste, and 
by the amount of funds available for 
such purchases. Generally purchases 
will be made only in areas in substantial 
compliance with the Department’s acre­
age recommendations. In order to en­
courage better grading and marketing 
practices, however, consideration will be 
given to areas substantially exceeding 
the suggested acreage: Provided, That 
such areas are following superior grading 
or marketing practices or can show def­
inite improvements in these respects. 
Grades and other specifications, and 
purchase prices will be contained in pur­
chase announcements which will be is­
sued to cover particular purchase opera­
tions. Information as to such purchase 
operations may be obtained by writing 
to the Fruit and Vegetable Branch, Pro­
duction and Marketing Administration, 
Department of Agriculture, Washington 
25; D. C.
(Sec. 32, 49 Stat. 774, as amended; 7 U. S. C.  
and Sup., 612c)
Done at Washington, D. C., this 11th 
day of October 1950.
[ seal ] s . R. S m it h,
Director,
Fruit and Vegetable Branch.

Franklin  D  Roosevelt

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Amendment  op Executive  O rder N o. 8283 
of November 9,1939, Amending  Section 
6 of Civil  Service Rule  n
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403), it 
is ordered that the penultimate para­
graph of Executive Order No. 8283 of
November 9, 1939, be, and it is hereby, 
amended to read*as follows:
“The second proviso  of the said section 
6 of Civil Service Rule n  as herein 
amended shall also apply to the incum­
bents of positions heretofore or here­
after covered into the classified (competi­
tive) service by section 1  of Executive 
Order No. 7916 of June 24, 1938, and sec­
tion 3 of that order is modified accord­
ingly, effective as of November 9, 1939.”
This order is recommended by the Civil 
Service Commission.
Franklin  D R oosevelt
The W hite  H ouse,
March 4, 1940.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Revocation  of E xecutive  O rder N o. 5346 
of M ay 9, 1930, W ithdrawing  P ublic  
Lands
MINNESOTA
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the act of June 25, 1910, c. 421, 36 
Stat. 847, Executive Order No. 5346 of 
May 9, 1930, withdrawing public lands in 
Minnesota pending a resurvey, is hereby 
revoked.
This order shall become effective upon 
the date of the official filing of the plat 
of the resurvey of the lands involved.
Franklin  D R oosevelt 
The W hite H ouse,
March 4, 1940.

I read the complete held EO 8854 (6 FR 4181, Aug. 16, 1941), titled 'Revoking Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, and Withdrawing the Land Released Thereby and Other Land ...': para. 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 'is hereby revoked', with no condition, exception or savings language, and para. 2 separately withdraws and reserves the same lands plus an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.","rationale":"I read the complete held EO 8751 (6 FR 2301, May 7, 1941): establishes the Division of Defense Aid Reports in the Office for Emergency Management, its Executive Officer, duties (sec. 2) and administrative arrangements; no own term (the machine 'condition' hit at sec. 2 is the 'subject to such policies as the President may prescribe' wording, not a term). I read the held EO 8926 (6 FR 5519, Oct. 30, 1941, signed Oct. 28, 1941, 'Establishing the Office of Lend-Lease Administration'): sec. 1 creates the Office of Lend-Lease Administration and sec. 5 states 'Executive Order No. 8751 of May 2, 1941, establishing the Division of Defense Aid Reports and defining its functions and duties, is hereby revoked.' The revocation is express and whole, with no savings clause. Earlier endings: none; the order was not amended in the history. I read the held EO 9243 text (7 FR 7213, September 12, 1942): paragraph 3 states 'Executive Order No. 8973 of December 12, 1941, and Executive Order No. 9067 of February 20, 1942, are hereby revoked, effective on the fifteenth day following the date of this order; provided that nothing contained in this order shall be construed to affect reemployment rights theretofore acquired by any employee under Executive Orders Nos. 8973 and 9067'. The proviso protects rights already acquired, not continued operation of EO 9067. EO 9695 (1946) later revoked EO 9243 and says nothing reviving EO 9067; EO 9952 and EO 9994 (held) state that the remaining reemployment rights expire, which is corroborative. I did not use the ACT records that rely on APP copies. Catalog note and 1989 snapshot are editorial leads. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.","rationale":"I read the complete held EO 9301 (8 FR 1825, Feb. 9, 1943, 'Establishing a Minimum Wartime Work-Week of Forty-Eight Hours'): para. 1 sets the 48-hour minimum workweek 'for the duration of the war', paras. 2-4 bind agencies and contractors and give the War Manpower Commission Chairman interpretive and regulatory power, para. 5 is a non-conflict clause for hours and wage laws. It has no dated term; the 'duration of the war' wording is the only own-term. I read the complete held EO 9607 (10 FR, Aug. 31, 1945, 'Revoking Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 1943'): its one operative sentence orders that 'Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 1943, establishing a minimum wartime workweek of forty-eight hours, be, and it is hereby, revoked', with no condition, exception or savings language, so the whole order ended on signing, Aug. 30, 1945. D6 self-check: the catalog 'See: EO 9333' cross-reference is a mismatch (EO 9333 is a Civil Service Schedule A amendment; I read the held pages). The only other held order that names EO 9301 is EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration for War, Apr. 19, 1943), which merely says solid-fuels directives must not conflict with WMC directives issued under EO 9301 and amends nothing; it predates the revocation and cannot revive the order. Other numeric hits in the corpus (EO 10366, 10648) are Federal Register page numbers. No held later instrument revives or re-enacts the workweek rule. The 'duration of the war' term could not have ended before the Aug. 30, 1945 revocation on any reading that I can support from the held record (formal war-termination proclamations came later), so no earlier own-term ending changes the NO. So the sec. 7 proviso text ended before EO 9830. EO 9721 (1946-05-10, held EO_9721.txt) only refers to sec. 6 (not a change). EO 9758 (CSC temporary regulations, in held issue) cites secs. 6 and 8 (not a change). Searched held FR texts 1946-1947 for 9691 (OCR-tolerant): only these and EO 9830. OWN-TERM / DEADLINE ITEMS (not decided): sec. 3 proviso (recommendations for a general revision of the Civil Service Rules 'not later than July 1, 1946') and sec. 7 first sentence (recommendations for a general revision of Schedule A 'before July 1, 1946') are report deadlines; whether they end anything turns on the pending owner ruling 'report-deadline', which is not decided here. Sec. 3 'transitional period until such time as the Civil Service Rules are revised' and sec. 4 'Pending the establishment of appropriate registers' are conditional own terms (leads). Sec. 9 revokes EO 9063, 9378 and 8514 (one-time act, executed on signing). EO 9830 is the whole-order revocation; it is not the first end of the sec. 7 proviso. - **ACT:EO:10161>EO:10219@58d721b452c686ea**; S52abd0c8dd79f14b5b35b878; {"actor_id":"EO:10219","char_end":18418,"char_start":18060,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2567,"char_start":1950,"text":"EXECUTIVE ORDER 10219\nD efining  C ertain R esponsibilities  of \nF ederal A gencies W ith  R espect T o \nT ransportation and S torage\nBy virtue of the authority vested in me \nby the Constitution and statutes, includ­\ning the Defense Production Act of 1950, \nand as President of the United States \nand Commander-in-Chief of the armed \nforces, and in order to assure the \nadequacy and effective utilization of \ntransportation and storage facilities to\nmeet the needs of national defense and \nof domestic and foreign commerce, it is \nhereby ordered as follows:\nPART I — DOMESTIC TRANSPORTATION \nAND STORAGE\nS ection 101."},{"char_end":4804,"char_start":4188,"text":"(g) Cooperate with \"the Secretary of \nCommerce, the Secretary of Defense, \nand the Secretary of the Interior, to \nachieve the effective coordination of in­\nland and ocean transportation and the \nefficient operation of all port facilities\n(Continued on next page)\nCONTENTS\nTHE PRESIDENT\nExecutive Orders  \nAirspace reservation over Las \nVegas Project, Las Vegas, Nev.;\nestablishment_______________\nTransportation and storage; de­\nfining certain responsibilities of \nFederal agencies ____________\nEXECUTIVE AGENCIES\nAgriculture Department  \nSee Commodity Credit Corpora­\ntion; Production and Marketing \nAdministration."},{"char_end":11798,"char_start":10751,"text":"Title 3 page\nChapter II (Executive orders):\n10218 ___________________ 1983\n10219 .......................................- 1983\nTitle 5\nChapter I:\nPart 27 ________________-—  1985\nChapter II:\nPart 210--------  1986\nTitle 6\nChapter IV:\nPart 601- ---------  1987\nTitle 7\nChapter IX:\nPart 978 (proposed) -------------- 2005\nTitle 15\nChapter HI: *\nPart 371_........—........................ 1989\nPart 372 ___________________ 1989\nPart 373 __________  1989\nPart 398 _____________  1989\nTitle 16\nChapter I:\nPart 3 (2 documents) ----------- 1991\nTitle 32A\nChapter III (OPS):\nGCPR................  1994\nChapter VI (NPA):\nM-14_____  1996\nM-32______________________ 1999\nM-35__________    2000\nM-40______________________ 2001\nM-41______________  2002\nChapter VIII (DTA):\nDTA 1 ______-____________ 2004\nTitle 49\nChapter I:\nPart 95________   2005\nto meet military and civilian require­\nments.(h) Cooperate with the Secretary of \nDefense and the Administrator of Gen­\neral Services to achieve the effective co­\nordination and utilization of storage \nfacilities."},{"char_end":14087,"char_start":13890,"text":"Secretary of the Interior to achieve \nthe effective coordination of ocean and \ninland transportation and the efficient \noperation of all port facilities to meet \nmilitary and civilian requirements."},{"char_end":17524,"char_start":17317,"text":"(b) Formulate plans and programs, \nand take such actions, as may be desir­\nable for meeting such requirements and \nobtaining the most effective utilization of \nsuch facilities for national defense \npurposes."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10161>EO:10219@58d721b452c686ea","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; requirements."},{"char_end":8113,"char_start":7912,"text":"(b) Formulate plans and programs, and take such actions, as may be desirable for meeting such requirements and obtaining the most effective - **ACT:EO:10161>EO:10233**; S03859a28f26f9b43dd3119b3; {"actor_id":"EO:10233","char_end":2442,"char_start":2254,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":440,"char_start":159,"text":"WHEREAS the maintenance of effective wage stabilization imposes limitation on the processes of free collective bargaining, making necessary the development of machinery to facilitate the settlement of labor disputes in conjunction with the administration of wage stabilization; and"},{"char_end":3461,"char_start":3240,"text":"To the maximum extent consistent with the maintenance of effective economic stabilization, the provisions of this Part shall be administered in such a way as to preserve collective bargaining between labor and management."},{"char_end":5731,"char_start":5326,"text":"All orders, regulations, rules, certificates, directives, and other actions relating to any function affected by the amendment made by the provisions of section 1 of this Executive Order (including the appointments of members of the Board in office on the date hereof) shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended, revoked, or terminated under proper authority."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10161>EO:10233","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending asserted. provisions for  \nbacitracin-neomycin with vasoconstric­\ntor, which authorizes storage of solutions  \nprepared from the drug for a period of  \n3 weeks at room temperature if the per­\nson who requests certification has proved  \nhis drug to be stable for such period of  \ntime, shall become effective upon pub­\nlication in the F ederal  R egister , since \nboth the public and the affected industry  \nwill benefit by the earliest effective date,  \nand I so find."},{"char_end":214165,"char_start":214110,"text":"These revised rules shall be effective  \nM ay 31, 1953."},{"char_end":231139,"char_start":231062,"text":"C. 11a,  \n426, 707)\nThis regulation is effective June 19,  \n1953.\n[ seal ] H."},{"char_end":243046,"char_start":242564,"text":"Effective at 10:00 a. m. on the 35th  \nday alter the date of this order, any of  \nthe public lands at Elfin Cove, Alaska,  \ndescribed in paragraph 1  of this order,  \nwhich are occupied by holders of per­\nmits from the Department of Agricul­\nture, who own valuable improvements on  \nthe lands, are restored, subject to valid  \nexisting rights, for purchase- as home-  \nsites under section 10 of the act of May  \n14, 1898, as amended by the act of May  \n26, 1934 (48 Stat. 809; 48 U."},{"char_end":245031,"char_start":244362,"text":"(a) (1) All carriers subject to the pub­\nlishing rules contained in §§ 187.0-10  \n(Tariff Circular M F No. 2), 187.21-187.47  \n(M F  No. 3), and 186.0-186.15 (M P No.  \n3), and their duly appointed agents are  \nhereby authorized to publish the follow­\ning provisions in supplements announc­\ning suspension of the rates, fares and-  \nother provisions of tariffs and schedules:\nIf this supplement is not canceled on or  \nbefore (here insert date to which suspended),  \nthe effective date of the above-described  \nsuspended publication or publications re­\nmaining under suspension until that date  \nis hereby postponed to the date upon which  \nthis supplement is canceled."},{"char_end":245823,"char_start":245299,"text":"(2) If the Commission has requested  \nthat the effective date of suspended  \nmatter be postponed beyond the period  \nprescribed by its order, or orders, of  \nsuspension, or beyond the date to which  \npostponement has been made under the  \nauthority of this special permission, the  \ncarrier or publishing agent may within  \nthe period of suspension or postpone­\nment file a supplement making the  \nrequested postponement effective on  \nstatutory notice whenever practicable,  \nbut in no case on less than one day’s  \nnotice."},{"char_end":246218,"char_start":245824,"text":"(3) When the Commission has found  \njustified matter, the effective date of  \nwhich is under postponement by author­\nity of this permission, the carrier or pub­\nlishing agent may within that period of  \npostponement publish and file on not less \nthan one day’s notice, unless otherwise  \ndirected by the Commission, a supple­\nment or revised page establishing the  \nmatter thus found justified."},{"char_end":261216,"char_start":260911,"text":"(3) This order shall be effective from  \nthe date of issuance until and pending  \nfinal disposition of the indictment found  \nin the United States District Court, for  \nthe Eastern District of Louisiana, New  \nOrleans Division, charging Gustavo Perez  \nwith conspiracy to violate the Export  \nControl Act."},{"char_end":263390,"char_start":263331,"text":"This delegation shall be effective as  \nof the date hereof."},{"char_end":268458,"char_start":268140,"text":"At any time after June  \n29, 1953, said applications-déclarations,  \nas filed or as amended, may be granted  \nand permitted to become effective as  \nprovided in Rule U-23 of the rules and  \nregulations under the act, or the Com­\nmission may exempt such transactions as  \nprovided in Rules U-20 (a) and U-100  \nthereof."},{"char_end":277640,"char_start":277326,"text":"It is requested that the Commission’s  \norder herein make the necessary findings  \nand contain the recitals required by Sup­\nplement R issuance."}],"exceptions_text":["Except in instances wherein  \nthe provisions concerned are for any rea­\nson inapplicable as of the effective date  \nof Reorganization Plan - **ACT:EO:10161>EO:10480**; Safef03733705aa0d1b86c9ee; {"actor_id":"EO:10480","char_end":38615,"char_start":38514,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":17230,"char_start":17045,"text":"(b) Findings made under or pursuant \nto and for the purposes of section 101 (b)\nof the Act shall not be effective until \napproved by the Director of the Office \nof Defense Mobilization."},{"char_end":28547,"char_start":27957,"text":"(b) Consult with and advise each del­\negate of the Director of the Office of \nDefense Mobilization referred to in sec­\ntion 201 (a) of\"this order and each offi­\ncial of the Government exercising guar­\nantee or loan functions under Part III \nof this order concerning (1) the effect of \ncontemplated actions on labor supply \nand utilization, (2) the relation of labor \nsupply to materials and facilities re­\nquirements, (3) such other matters as \nwill assist in making the exercise of pri­\nority and allocations functions consis­\ntent with effective utilization a n d  \ndistribution of labor."},{"char_end":38457,"char_start":37991,"text":"All orders, regulations, rul­\nings, certificates, directives and other \nactions relating to any function affected \nby this order shall remain in effect ex­\ncept as they are inconsistent herewith \nor are hereafter amended or revoked \nunder proper authority, and nothing in \nthis order shall affect the validity or \nforce of anything heretofore done under \npreyious delegations or other assignment \n.of authority under the Defense Produc­\ntion Act of 1950, as amended."},{"char_end":39901,"char_start":39715,"text":"The \nfollowing designated orders, modified as \nrequired to conform them to the provi­\nsions of this order, shall remain in effect:\nExecutive Order No. 10182 of November  \n21, 1950 (15 F."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10161>EO:10480","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; R. 6105-6108, as amended, \nshall be, and it is hereby, further \namended by adding the following at the \nend of Part V thereof :\n“S ec. 503. (a) Except as otherwise \nprovided in section 503 (b) of this Ex­\necutive order, the functions conferred \nupon the President by section 607 of the \nDefense Production Act of 1950, as \namended, are hereby delegated to the \nBoard of Governors of the Federal Re­\nserve System. The Board shall perform \nthe functions delegated by this subsec­\ntion subject to the concurrence of the \nHousing and Home Finance Administra­\ntor and upon the basis of estimates made \npursuant to section 503 (b) of this \nExecutive order.\n“ (b) The Secretary of Labor shall, \npursuant to section 607 of the Defense \nProduction Act of 1950, as amended, \nmake estimates of the number of perma­\nnent, non-farm, family dwelling units \nthe construction of which has been \nstarted during each calendar month, \nand, on the basis of such estimates, make \nestimates of the annual rate of construc­\ntion starts during each such month, \nafter making reasonable allowance for \nseasonal variations in the rate of con­\nstruction. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"By virtue of the authority vested in me \nby the Defense Production Act of 1950, \nas amended (50 U. S. C. App. 2061 et \nseq.), and as President of the United \nStates, it is ordered that section 403 of \nExecutive Order No. 10161 of September \n9, 1950 (15 P. R. 6105), as amended, be, \nand it is hereby, further amended by \nredesignating paragraph (b) thereof as \nparagraph (c) and by inserting im­\nmediately after paragraph (a) thereof \nthe following new paragraph:\n“(b) In addition to the members of \nthe Wage Stabilization Board provided \nfor in section 403 (a) of this order, the \nBoard shall have not more than two \nalternate members who shall be repre­\nsentative of labor and not more than \ntwo alternate members who shall be \nrepresentative of business and industry. \nAlternate members shall be appointed \nby the President, by and with the advice \nand consent of the Senate, at such times \nas he may deem necessary. Any alter­\nnate member shall participate as a mem­\nber of the Board only in lieu of a member \nappointed under section 403 (a) of this \norder who is not participating, and only \nwhen called upon by the Chairman of the \nWage Stabilization Board to so partici­\npate, and when so participating each \nalternate member shall have the same \nstatus and functions as a member ap­\npointed under the said section 403 (a). \nThe designation by the Chairman of the \nBoard of alternate members to partici­\npate as members of the Board shall be \nso ordered as to preserve the equal rep- ' \nresentation required by the provisions of \nsection 403 (a) hereof and of section \n403 (b) of the Defense Production Act \nof 1950, as amended.”\nx  Harry S. - **ACT:EO:10193>EO:10219**; S87eacdfe58582d51ef93ba90; {"actor_id":"EO:10219","char_end":18418,"char_start":18060,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2567,"char_start":1950,"text":"EXECUTIVE ORDER 10219\nD efining  C ertain R esponsibilities  of \nF ederal A gencies W ith  R espect T o \nT ransportation and S torage\nBy virtue of the authority vested in me \nby the Constitution and statutes, includ­\ning the Defense Production Act of 1950, \nand as President of the United States \nand Commander-in-Chief of the armed \nforces, and in order to assure the \nadequacy and effective utilization of \ntransportation and storage facilities to\nmeet the needs of national defense and \nof domestic and foreign commerce, it is \nhereby ordered as follows:\nPART I — DOMESTIC TRANSPORTATION \nAND STORAGE\nS ection 101."},{"char_end":4804,"char_start":4188,"text":"(g) Cooperate with \"the Secretary of \nCommerce, the Secretary of Defense, \nand the Secretary of the Interior, to \nachieve the effective coordination of in­\nland and ocean transportation and the \nefficient operation of all port facilities\n(Continued on next page)\nCONTENTS\nTHE PRESIDENT\nExecutive Orders  \nAirspace reservation over Las \nVegas Project, Las Vegas, Nev.;\nestablishment_______________\nTransportation and storage; {"actor_id":"EO:10433","char_end":19020,"char_start":18744,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"stated_date","effective_date":"1953-06-19","effective_wording":[{"char_end":3437,"char_start":2957,"text":"The \nGovernment; and he shall establish such  \ninteragency committees and working  \ngroups composed of representatives of  \ninterested departments and agencies,  \nand consult with such departments and  \nagencies, as may be necessary for the  \nmost effective performance of his  \nfunctions."},{"char_end":18014,"char_start":17025,"text":"(a) Except in instances wherein  \nthe provisions concerned are for any rea­\nson inapplicable as of the effective date  \nof Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953,\n(1) each reference in any prior Execu­\ntive order to the Director of Defense  \nMobilization is hereby amended to refer  \nto the Director of the Office of Defense  \nMobilization provided for in Reorganiza­\ntion Plan No. 3 of 1953, and (2) each  \nreference in any prior Executive order\n3515\nto the Office of Defense Mobilization  \nshall hereafter be deemed to be a ref­\nerence to the Office of Defense Mobiliza­\ntion established by Reorganization Plan  \nNo. 3 of 1953.\ntb) Without limiting the application  \nof section 2 (a) of this order, the amend­\nments made thereby shall apply subject  \nto the provisions of the said section 2 (a ),  \nto prior references to the Director of  \nDefense Mobilization and the Office of  \nDefense Mobilization in the following  \nExecutive orders:\nExecutive Order No. 10161 of September 9,\n1950 (15 F."},{"char_end":19301,"char_start":19030,"text":"All orders, regulations, rulings,  \ncertificates, directives, and other actions  \nrelating to any function affected by this  \nExecutive order shall remain in effect  \nexcept as they are inconsistent herewith  \nor are hereafter amended or revoked  \nunder proper authority."},{"char_end":19967,"char_start":19746,"text":"The provisions of this Execu­\ntive order shall become effective when  \nthe first Director of the Office of Defense  \nMobilization appointed under Reorgani­\nzation Plan No. 3 of 1953 enters upon  \noffice’ as such Director."},{"char_end":57013,"char_start":56797,"text":"The maxi­\nmum amount of cotton stored in any  \nstructure shall be limited to 200 bales,  \nunless the State committee determines  \nthat a larger maximum is required to  \nmake the program more effective in the  \nState."},{"char_end":61719,"char_start":61238,"text":"Such charges, accrued through  \nJuly 31 of any year in which these rates  \nare in effect, shall be paid by CCC, as  \nsoon as possible after such date, on all  \nof the cotton represented by warehouse  \nreceipts held by CCC at the time of pay­\nment; Provided,  That on any cotton for  \nwhich CCC makes payment of accrued  \ncharges through July 31 of any year, pay­\nment for the fractional part of a month  \nprior to such date shall be at the propor­\ntionate part of the monthly rate."},{"char_end":63378,"char_start":62140,"text":"All other charges on  \ncotton, including compression charges,  \nand flat delivery charges on cotton moved  \nfrom a warehouse operating compress  \nfacilities without payment of compres­\nsion charges, wifi be at the rates provided  \nin the warehouseman’s established tariff  \nin effect at the time the service is ordered  \nperformed: Provided,  That no charge  \nmay be made with respect to the cotton  \nthat is not applicable to cotton other  \nthan CCC loan cotton stored by the  \nwarehouseman, except that the ware­\nhouseman may make a charge of not to  \nexceed 35 cents per bale for transmitting  \nsamples to the designated classing office, \npostage, verifying and guaranteeing the  \ncorrectness of the information for which  \nthe warehouse is responsible in the\nSchedule of Pledged Cotton on the Form  \nA  or Form G -l, and executing the Agree­\nment of Warehouseman on the Form A  \nor the Warehouseman’s Certificate and  \nAgreement on the Form G -l, if such  \ncharges are included in the warehouse­\nman’s tariff: And provided further,  That \nin no event shall such charge, a service  \ncharge, or charges for receiving, tagging,  \nweighing, sampling on arrival, or storage  \nof samples be collected from CCC or a \npurchaser of the cotton."},{"char_end":65227,"char_start":64775,"text":"In the event that the cotton is pur­\nchased or pooled by CCC or the loan on  \nsuch cotton is extended or carried in  \npast-due status by CCC after July 3 1 ,  \n1954, the rates quoted herein will remain \nin effect until terminated by CCC O r the \nwarehouseman at the end of any month  \nby giving the other at least 30 days’  \nnotice, or until the cotton comes under  \nanother storage agreement between the  \nwarehouseman and CCC, whichever is  \nearlier."},{"char_end":86670,"char_start":85939,"text":"(l) Pursuant to the marketing  \nagreement, as amended, and Order No.  \n3 6 , as amended (7 CFR Part 936), regu­\nlating the handling of fresh Bartlett  \nPears, plums, and Elberta peaches grown  \nin the State of California, effective under  \nthe applicable provisions of the Agri­\ncultural Marketing Agreement Act of  \n1 9 3 7 , as amended, and upon the basis of \nthe recommendations of the Plum Com­\nmodity Committee, established under  \nthe aforesaid amended marketing agree-\nment and order, and upon other avail­\nable information, it is hereby found that  \nthe limitation of shipments of plums of  \nthe variety hereinafter set forth, and in  \nthe manner herein provided, will tend  \nto effectuate the declared policy of the  \nact."},{"char_end":86979,"char_start":86671,"text":"(2) It is hereby further found that  \nit is impracticable and contrary to the  \npublic interest to give preliminary  \nnotice, engage in public rule making  \nprocedure, and postpone the effective  \ndate of this section until 30 days after  \npublication thereof in the F ederal R eg­\nister  (60 Stat. 237; 5 U."},{"char_end":87492,"char_start":86983,"text":"C. 1001  \net seq.) in that, as hereinafter set forth,  \nthe time policy of the act is insufficient ;  \na reasonable time is permitted, under  \nthe circumstances, for preparation for  \nsuch effective time; and good cause  \nexists for making the provisions of this  \nsection effective not later than June 20,  \n1953."},{"char_end":88520,"char_start":87493,"text":"A reasonable determination as  \nto the supply of, and the demand for,  \nsuch plums must the extent of, regula­\ntion of shipments of such plums was  \nmade at the meeting of said committee  \non June 12, 1953, after consideration of  \nall available information relative to the  \nsupply and demand conditions for such  \nplums, at which time the recommenda­\ntion and supporting information was  \nsubmitted to the Department; ship­\nments of the current crop of such plums  \nare expected to begin on or about June  \n21, 1953, and this section should be ap­\nplicable to all such shipments of such  \nplums in order to effectuaté the declared  \npolicy of the act; and compliance with  \nthe provisions of this section will not  \nrequire of handlers any preparation  \ntherefor which cannot be completed by  \nthe effective time of this   Text: [Tc706f6f779d884ec084ed751](#tc706f6f779d884ec084ed751); absolute characters 2294–2558
- **ACT:EO:10193>EO:10480**; Scbd474a7e330825440c6ac32; {"actor_id":"EO:10480","char_end":25004,"char_start":24758,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":4285,"char_start":4103,"text":"(b) Findings made under or pursuant to and for the purposes of section 101 (b) of the Act shall not be effective until approved by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization."},{"char_end":15211,"char_start":14646,"text":"(b) Consult with and advise each delegate of the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization referred to in section 201 (a) of this order and each official of the Government exercising guarantee or loan functions under Part HI of this order concerning (1) the effect of contemplated actions on labor supply and utilization, (2) the relation of labor supply to materials and facilities requirements, (3) such other matters as will assist in making the exercise of priority and allocations functions consistent with effective utilization and distribution of labor."},{"char_end":24756,"char_start":24305,"text":"All orders, regulations, rulings, certificates, directives and other actions relating to any function affected by this order shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended or revoked under proper authority, and nothing in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything heretofore done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended."},{"char_end":26072,"char_start":25946,"text":"The following designated orders, modified as required to conform them to the provisions of this order, shall remain in effect:"}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10193>EO:10480","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending asserted. special order which either adds an  \narticle to those already listed in the  \nwholesaler’ s application or changes the  \nretail ceiling price of a listed article, the  \napplicant named in this special order  \nmust comply, as to each such article,  \nwith the preticketing requirements of  \nthis paragraph within 30 days after the  \neffective date of the amendment."},{"char_end":130764,"char_start":130597,"text":"After  \n60 days from the effective date, no re-  \ntalier may offer or sell the article unless  \nit is ticketed in accordance with the re­\nquirements of this paragraph."},{"char_end":131324,"char_start":131009,"text":"Within 15 days after the effective  \ndate of this special order, the wholesaler  \nshall send a copy of this special order  \nto each purchaser for resale to whom,  \nwithin two months immediately prior to  \nthe effective date, the wholesaler had  \ndelivered any article covered in para­\ngraph 1 of this special order."},{"char_end":131620,"char_start":131325,"text":"Copies  \nshall also be sent to all other purchasers  \non or before the date of the first delivery  \nof any such article subsequent to the  \neffective date of this special order, and  \nshall be accompanied by copies of each  \namendment thereto (if any) issued prior  \nto the date of the delivery."},{"char_end":132439,"char_start":132186,"text":"Within 15 days after the effective date  \nof this special order, two copies of this  \nnotice must be also be filed by the whole­\nsaler with the Distribution Price Branch,  \nConsumer Soft Goods Division, Office of  \nPrice Stabilization, Washington 25, D."},{"char_end":132811,"char_start":132445,"text":"Within 15 days after the effective date  \nof any subsequent amendment to this  \nspecial order, the wholesaler shall send  \na copy of the amendment to each pur­\nchaser to whom, within 2 months im­\nmediately prior to the effective date of  \nsuch amendment, the wholesaler had  \ndelivered any article the sale of which  \nis affected in any manner by the amend­\nment.\n5."},{"char_end":133120,"char_start":132812,"text":"Within 45 days of the expiration  \nof the first 6-month period following  \nthe effective date of this special order  \nand within 45 days of the expiration of  \neach successive 6-month period, the  \nwholesaler shall file with the Distribution  \nPrice Branch, Office of Price Stabiliza­\ntion, Washington 25, D."},{"char_end":133776,"char_start":133761,"text":"Effective date."},{"char_end":133838,"char_start":133778,"text":"This special order  \nshall become effective August 23, larger maximum is required to  \nmake the program more effective in the  \nState."},{"char_end":61719,"char_start":61238,"text":"Such charges, accrued through  \nJuly 31 of any year in which these rates  \nare in effect, shall be paid by CCC, as  \nsoon as possible after such date, on all  \nof the cotton represented by warehouse  \nreceipts held by CCC at the time of pay­\nment; Provided,  That on any cotton for  \nwhich CCC makes payment of accrued  \ncharges through July 31 of any year, pay­\nment for the fractional part of a month  \nprior to such date shall be at the propor­\ntionate part of the monthly rate."},{"char_end":63378,"char_start":62140,"text":"All other charges on  \ncotton, including compression charges,  \nand flat delivery charges on cotton moved  \nfrom a warehouse operating compress  \nfacilities without payment of compres­\nsion charges, wifi be at the rates provided  \nin the warehouseman’s established tariff  \nin effect at the time the   Text: [Te62492c8955daaf154ea25ee](#te62492c8955daaf154ea25ee); absolute characters 13066–14608
- **ACT:EO:10200>EO:10480**; Scbd474a7e330825440c6ac32; {"actor_id":"EO:10480","char_end":25071,"char_start":24758,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":4285,"char_start":4103,"text":"(b) Findings made under or pursuant to and for the purposes of section 101 (b) of the Act shall not be effective until approved by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization."},{"char_end":15211,"char_start":14646,"text":"(b) Consult with and advise each delegate of the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization referred to in section 201 (a) of this order and each official of the Government exercising guarantee or loan functions under Part HI of this order concerning (1) the effect of contemplated actions on labor supply and utilization, (2) the relation of labor supply to materials and facilities requirements, (3) such other matters as will assist in making the exercise of priority and allocations functions consistent with effective utilization and distribution of labor."},{"char_end":24756,"char_start":24305,"text":"All orders, regulations, rulings, certificates, directives and other actions relating to any function affected by this order shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended or revoked under proper authority, and nothing in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything heretofore done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended."},{"char_end":26072,"char_start":25946,"text":"The following designated orders, modified as required to conform them to the provisions of this order, shall remain in effect:"}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10200>EO:10480","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"SEC 606.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"whole","signing_date":"1953-08-14","target_id":"EO:10200","verb":"supersede"}

S. C. App. 2061 et \nseq.), and as President of the United \nStates, it is ordered that section 403 of \nExecutive Order No. 10161 of September \n9, 1950 (15 P. R. 6105), as amended, be, \nand it is hereby, further amended by \nredesignating paragraph (b) thereof as \nparagraph (c) and by inserting im­\nmediately after paragraph (a) thereof \nthe following new paragraph:\n“(b) In addition to the members of \nthe Wage Stabilization Board provided \nfor in section 403 (a) of this order, the \nBoard shall have not more than two \nalternate members who shall be repre­\nsentative of labor and not more than \ntwo alternate members who shall be \nrepresentative of business and industry. \nAlternate members shall be appointed \nby the President, by and with the advice \nand consent of the Senate, at such times \nas he may deem necessary.   Text: [Te62492c8955daaf154ea25ee](#te62492c8955daaf154ea25ee); absolute characters 13066–14608

- **ACT:EO:10483>EO:10700@14cf3252d7bf69a5**; S8ef665e04f493a553f53f9a8; {"actor_id":"EO:10700","char_end":4621,"char_start":4239,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"stated_date","effective_date":"1957-07-01","effective_wording":[{"char_end":676,"char_start":237,"text":"(a) In order to assist in the effective coordination among certain agencies of certain functions relating to the national security and to provide for the integrated implementation of national security policies by the said agencies, there is hereby established within the structure of the National Security Council the Operations Coordinating Board, hereinafter referred to as the Board, which shall report to the National Security Council."},{"char_end":4621,"char_start":4239,"text":"(b) Members of the staff of the Operations Coordinating Board provided for in Executive Order No. 10483, as amended, who are immediately prior to the taking effect of this order receiving compensation directly out of funds available to the said Board shall be transferred to the staff of the Board referred to in paragraph (a) of this section as of the effective date of this order."},{"char_end":6634,"char_start":6275,"text":"The foregoing provisions of this order shall become effective on July 1, 1957, except that if funds appropriated for the National Security Council shall not have become available on that date for the support of the Board in consonance with this order, the said provisions shall become effective on such later date as funds so appropriated become so available."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10483>EO:10700@14cf3252d7bf69a5","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending asserted. Effective date depends on agency, publication or an unstated event.","provision_label":"","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["Doc. 59-5408; Filed, ' June 26, 1959;\n8:53 a.m.]\nFEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE \nCORPORATION\n[12 CFR Part 329 1\nPAYMENT OF DEPOSITS AND INTER­\nEST THEREON BY INSURED NON­\nMEMBER BANKS\nNotice of Proposed Rule Making\nPart 329 of the rules and regulations of  \nthe Federal Deposit Insurance Corpora­\ntion, relating to the payment of deposits  \nand interest thereon, provides in  \n§  329.3(c) that insured nonmember  \nbanks may pay interest at the applicable  \nmaximum rate from the first day of the  \nmonth on a savings deposit received  \nduring the first 10 business days of any  \ncalendar month commencing a quarterly  \nor semiannual interest period, and dur­\ning the first 5 business days of any  \nother calendar month.","The Board of Directors of the Federal  \nDeposit Insurance Corporation is con­\nsidering amending §  329.3(c) so as to  \npermit insured nonmember banks to pay  \ninterest at the maximum permissible  \nrate from the first day of the month on  \nsavings deposits received during the first  \n10 calendar days in any month.","The purpose of this amendment is to  \nreduce misunderstandings in connection  \nwith these so-called “grace periods,”  \nmake possible uniform advertising,  \ncreate better customer relationships, and  \nenable banks that compute interest on a  \ncycle basis to facilitate computation of  \ninterest on savings accounts and elimi­\nnate difficulties presently being en­\ncountered.","The proposed amendment would  \nchange §  329.3(c) to read as follows:\n(c) Grace periods in computing inter­\nest on savings deposits.","An insured \nnonmember bank may pay interest on a  \nsavings deposit received during the first  \nten (10) calendar days of any calendar  \nmonth at the applicable maximum rate  \nprescribed pursuant to paragraph (a) of  \nthis section calculated from the first day  \nof such calendar month until such  \ndeposit is withdrawn or ceases to con­\nstitute a savings deposit under the pro­\nvisions of this part, whichever shall first  \noccur; and an insured nonmember bank  \nmay pay interest on a savings deposit  \nwithdrawn during i,ts last three (3) busi­\nness days of any calendar month ending  \na regular quarterly or semiannual inter­\nest period at the applicable maximum  \nrate prescribed pursuant to paragraph  \n(a) of this section calculated to the end  \nof such calendar month.","Q]\nPAYMENT OF INTEREST ON DEPOSITS\nNotice of Proposed Rule Making\nPart 217 (Regulation Q ), relating to  \nthe payment of interest on deposits pro­\nvides in §  217.3(d) that member banks  \nmay compute interest at the applicable  \nmaximum rate from the first day of the  \nmonth on a savings deposit received dur­\ning the first 10 business days of any cal­\nendar month commencing a quarterly or  \nsemi-annual interest period, and during\nFEDERAL REGISTER\nthe first five business days of any other  \ncalendar month.","The Board is considering amending  \nthis subsection so as to permit member  \nbanks to pay interest at the maximum  \npermissible rate from the first day of the  \nmonth on savings deposits received dur­\ning the first 10 calendar days in any  \nmonth.","The proposed amendment to §  217.3 is \nas follows:\n(d) Grace periods in computing inter­\nest on savings deposits.","A member bank  \nmay pay interest on a savings deposit  \nreceived during the first 10 calendar days  \nof any calendar month at the applicable  \nmaximum rate prescribed pursuant to  \nparagraph (a) of this section calculated  \nfrom the first day of such calendar month  \nuntil such deposit is withdrawn or ceases  \nto constitute a savings deposit under the  \nprovisions of this part, whichever shall  \nfirst occur; and a member bank may pay\n^  5251\ninterest on a savings deposit withdrawn  \nduring  \ncalculated to the end of such Calendar  \nmonth. ^\nThis notice is published pursuant to  \nsection 4 of the Administrative Proce­\ndure Act and section 2 of the rules of  \nprocedure of the Board
